note: Filled in from docs/accessibility-assessment.md after each round of testing. A test without its own environment and date used the shared run.

run.environment: Chrome 156 on macOS (Apple silicon), driven by script.

done.result: axe-core 4.11 ran on every page, at phone and desktop widths, in light and dark schemes, and with each calculator showing a result and an error. It found no violations. Where it could not judge the contrast of some text, a script measured each case, and none was below the required ratio.
At 320 CSS pixels wide, no page scrolls sideways. Wide tables and charts scroll inside their own area.
With the spacing of WCAG 1.4.12 applied, no text was cut off on any page.
No control is smaller than 24 by 24 CSS pixels, apart from links inside a sentence, which the guidelines exempt. Some controls are between 24 and 43 pixels high, below our own aim of 44.
A script pressed Tab through every page. Every control was reached, in reading order, with an outline style set when focused, and none was covered by other content.
No page skips a heading level.

Every explanation can be read. With JavaScript off, each calculator shows a notice instead of its form, and none of the sentences that tell a reader what to enter or copy. The triple lock calculator, the rule comparison and the history explorer also show a default result; the budget explorer's notice points to its example budgets, set out in full on its page. Each calculator was also loaded with its own script blocked, when the notice adds that the script did not run and how to report it, and with its script held back, when neither the form nor the notice shows until it runs.

done.check: VoiceOver with Safari on a Mac
done.result: A person listened to every page from top to foot, with every disclosure open, and listed each page's headings, tables, links and landmarks; worked through the four calculators, hearing entered figures, errors, results, charts and their tables, and a copied link; and moved through every table by row and by column. What was found was fixed and heard again.
done.environment: Safari with VoiceOver on macOS, used by a person.

done.check: VoiceOver with Safari on an iPhone
done.result: A person worked through the triple lock calculator. What was found was fixed and checked again, apart from the two points listed under what has not been tested.
done.environment: Safari with VoiceOver on iOS, used by a person.

done.result: A person tested the site with a keyboard alone, in Chrome and then in Firefox. Two faults were found and fixed: the "Back to top" link could not be reached with Tab, and the history explorer's copy button gave no visible sign that it had worked.
done.environment: Chrome and Firefox on macOS, used by a person.

done.result: A person zoomed every page to 200% and 400% in Chrome, and the costs page and the budget explorer to 400% in Firefox. One fault was found and fixed: on the costs page, the outline of a focused table covered the first letter of its caption.
done.environment: Chrome and Firefox on macOS, used by a person.

not_done.check: VoiceOver on an iPhone for the other three calculators
not_done.reason: On an iPhone the budget explorer, the rule comparison and the history explorer have not been tested. On the triple lock calculator on an iPhone, one paragraph was read twice on one pass, which could not be repeated, and VoiceOver read the summary "At a glance" after each digit typed. Both are still to be looked at.
NVDA is a free screen reader for Windows. Not yet tested. No Windows computer was available.

not_done.check: Touch on a phone without a screen reader
not_done.reason: Tested at phone width on a computer, and on an iPhone only with VoiceOver, as above.

not_done.check: The automated and scripted checks in Firefox and Safari
not_done.reason: They used Chrome only. Firefox was used for the keyboard and zoom checks, and Safari with VoiceOver, as above.

not_done.check: Use by disabled and older readers
not_done.reason: We have held no usability sessions.
No one has carried one out.

not_done.check: The "Out of date" note in the calculators
not_done.reason: Added on 5 October 2026. When a figure is half typed, the last result stays with this note. It was looked at in screenshots. On the rule comparison, VoiceOver with Safari on a Mac said the field, what to enter and that the result shown is out of date on leaving a wrong figure. The note has not been heard in the other calculators, and the automated rules did not scan that state.

not_done.check: Changes to a form when a choice is made
not_done.reason: Some choices change other fields at once: the household, the budget period, the scenario, the number of years, the first year and the pension series. With VoiceOver, choosing a household said nothing of the field it adds or empties; it now says so. A person has not yet judged whether each change is clear.
